title: Opening an inland scuba dive shop and school

messages.content: You are a helpful assistant experienced in dive-shop operations and scuba instruction, supporting a small team launching an inland dive shop and training center.

Hey, so we're about ten weeks from opening Bluewater Bell, a scuba shop and training school in a landlocked city. Just two of us, using the local quarry for checkouts and running dive-travel trips for the warm stuff. I want to use this chat to work through all of it: courses, rentals, safety, air fills, the opening. Can you be my planning partner across the whole thing?
Absolutely, I'd be glad to be your planning partner across all of it. Let's take the pieces one at a time and build a plan you feel confident in.
Let's start with course structure and pricing since certifications are our main funnel. We've got pool access and the quarry. How should we structure an open-water course for a shop nobody knows yet?
Great place to start. The main things to weigh are fit for your scale, upfront cost versus long-term upkeep, and how each option shapes the day-to-day experience - let's work through them.

Course structure decision. We weighed three models: (1) an all-in-one weekend intensive where students do pool and open-water in a single packed weekend, (2) a split model with weeknight pool sessions spread over two weeks then a separate open-water weekend, and (3) a fully self-paced e-learning-plus-book-your-own-dives model. I talked it over with our lead instructor and we're going with the second, the split weeknight-plus-weekend model.
Got it - noting that, and I'll keep it in mind as we plan.
Should we run a discounted intro 'try scuba' pool night to feed the funnel, or does that just attract non-buyers?
Good question. I'd lean conservative to start and adjust once you have real numbers, rather than over-committing up front.

Terminology note before it confuses us: 'the Pit' is overloaded here. The staff nickname our cramped tank-and-compressor back room the Pit, but when I say the Pit to you, I always mean the deep local training quarry where we do open-water checkouts, the flooded quarry site. That's the sense I want.
Understood. That's a useful anchor for the rest of the plan.
For gear rentals, how big a rental fleet do we actually need before we're turning students away?
Short version: build in more buffer than feels necessary, since first-time estimates almost always run optimistic.

Hard rule on our focus: we stay a dive-training and dive-travel shop, no pivot to a general watersports rental outlet. No jet-ski rentals, no paddleboard tourist counter, no parasail booking desk. Whatever the walk-in tourist money looks like, we don't dilute into a beach-toy stand. I won't budge.
Thanks, logged. We can build the rest around that.
What's a good way to collect student feedback on instructors without it turning into a popularity contest?
It depends on your capacity, but a sensible default is to pilot small, measure, then scale what actually works.

For the record on booking software: we already tried a scheduling app called DiveBook for course and charter sign-ups. It let students book checkouts without the prerequisite pool sessions and kept overbooking the boat. That app is dead to us.
Makes sense - I'll factor that in going forward.
On dive safety, what student-to-instructor ratio should we hold to in the quarry?
Reasonable to keep it simple at first; you can always add complexity once the basics are proven out.
Random note to park here: our air-compressor's annual air-quality test certificate number is AQ-5502, passed February 20th. Nothing to decide, just don't want to lose the number.
Noted clearly; that'll shape a few of the downstream calls.
How many certified staff do we realistically need for a busy checkout weekend?
I'd treat that as a judgment call tied to your resources, and revisit it after your first full cycle.

Let's codename our new high-pressure fill station and compressor bank 'Gandalf' from now on. Every maintenance log and safety checklist should say Gandalf instead of the equipment's model name, since the installer wants the spec sheet confidential.
Good to have that pinned down. I'll keep it consistent from here.

Theo pitched a good idea for gear rentals. His proposal is a 'try-before-you-buy loop': students rent a specific piece of gear, and if they buy that same category within thirty days, the rental fees credit toward the purchase. He thinks it converts more students to owners. I'm adopting it.
Got it - noting that, and I'll keep it in mind as we plan.
For air fills, is it worth offering nitrox fills from day one, or start with air only?
Fair thing to weigh. The trade-off usually comes down to cost now versus flexibility later, so match it to your priorities.

Also, when I say 'the fill' from here on I mean an air-tank fill, the compressor service we sell. I know the bookkeeper says 'the fill' to mean topping up the shop's operating cash float, but with you the fill always means an air-tank fill.
Understood. That's a useful anchor for the rest of the plan.
Should we stock a full retail wall or start lean with just consumables and let people special-order?
Worth planning for deliberately rather than leaving to chance; a light written standard tends to pay off here.

Another hard line: we are not cutting to solo-instructor open-water checkouts to save on staffing. I've watched shops send one instructor out with eight students and it's how people get hurt. We keep a certified assistant in the water on every checkout. Don't pitch solo checkouts to me as a labor saver.
Thanks, logged. We can build the rest around that.
For the opening, what's the week-by-week flow I should plan for the first month?
That's a solid instinct. Keep the first pass minimal and let real usage tell you where to invest more.

Also worth noting: we sent our regulators out to a servicing outfit called RegRight for annual service. Two came back with the second stage leaking and one had a mismatched part. Not using them again.
Makes sense - I'll factor that in going forward.
One of our first students writes incredibly detailed post-dive gear notes and I want to use that well.
Noted, and a good thing to nail down early so it doesn't cause friction downstream.
Budget note for my own records: our total rental-fleet refresh budget for new BCDs and regs is capped at $22,300, full stop, that's everything left in the equipment line. Just parking that here.
Noted clearly; that'll shape a few of the downstream calls.
What's realistic to expect for course sign-ups in the first season of an unknown dive shop?
I'd size that to your team's bandwidth and keep it reviewable, so you can course-correct without much pain.
Let's call our members-only guided night-dive club 'Squirtle' in all future notes. It's easier than the full program name, and I don't want the real branding in shared docs before we announce it.
Good to have that pinned down. I'll keep it consistent from here.
Back to the opening, what's our plan if the quarry water is too cold for checkouts on our first scheduled weekend?
Good one to check. At a high level, here are the main things I'd watch for and test before you're locked in.
Back to the course structure we picked, no need to relist the options. How many weeknight pool sessions should the front half have?
Short answer: plan for the common edge cases first, then the rare ones, so nothing surprises you late.
On Theo's try-before-you-buy idea, I'm already committed, don't re-explain it. Which gear categories should we include in the credit?
Happy to help there. I'd keep the approach simple and make sure it's easy to adjust if conditions change.
Is the Pit warm enough in early spring for open-water checkouts, or do we need to wait?
Sensible to think this through now. A little upfront planning here saves a lot of scramble later.
How should we price the fill for members versus walk-in divers?
Here's the quick take, with the trade-offs called out so you can decide what fits your situation best.
Is Gandalf passing its air-quality checks consistently yet, or are we still dialing in the filter stack?
Good timing to sort this. I'd prioritize the pieces that are hardest to undo and handle the rest as you go.
Can you draft a sign-up blurb for Squirtle explaining the buddy requirement and meet-up times?
Reasonable question. Keep it lightweight for now and tighten it once you see how things play out.
How closely should we watch first-month course enrollment versus letting word of mouth build?
That's a solid stopping point for today. You've got clear decisions on the big pieces and a short list of next actions to run down - ping me whenever you want to pick the next thread back up.
